findings.title: [A01/CWE-841] `pass_check`/`reject_check` enforce no state precondition — a REVIEWER can mark never-entered equipment CONFIRMED and bypass the entire designer-submit + deviation gate
findings.why_it_matters: The four-eyes control this router exists to enforce is bypassable by any user holding the REVIEWER role alone. `check_actual_data` loads the equipment and calls `pass_check_svc` unconditionally; `pass_check` writes `actual_data_status = CONFIRMED` and flushes with no check on the current status. A REVIEWER who has project access can therefore drive an equipment from `NOT_ENTERED` (no designer ever typed a single value, no deviation report ever generated, no designer ever submitted) straight to `CONFIRMED`, and the router returns 200 with `actual_data_status: "CONFIRMED"`. The downstream effect is not cosmetic: `pass_check` fires the `actual_data_replaces_design` event with `before=equipment.design_parameters_json` and `after=equipment.actual_data_json` — for a never-entered machine `after` is `None` — and the confirmation gate (`can_confirm`, the whole fail-closed deviation engine of S4-2) lives only in `confirm_actual_data`, which this path never reaches. The resulting `CONFIRMED` status is exactly what `record_actual_data` treats as the lock that forbids re-entry (`ACTUAL_DATA_LOCKED`), so the equipment is permanently frozen against the designer who was supposed to fill it in. `reject_check` has the mirror-image gap: it resets a `CONFIRMED` record to `PENDING_CONFIRM` with no precondition, which unlocks the re-entry channel on any record. The fix is the repo's own guard pattern applied at the service boundary — raise `PcsError(409/422, ...)` when `equipment.actual_data_status` is not `PENDING_CONFIRM` before either transition, mirroring how `record_actual_data` already gates on `CONFIRMED`.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/supplier.py:210 — `    record = await _load_equipment(db, equipment_id, actor)` / `211` `if body.decision == "pass":` / `212` `await pass_check_svc(db, record, actor, reason=body.reason)` — no status argument is passed and no status assertion precedes the call; the endpoint's only gate is `require_roles(actor, *_CHECK_ROLES)` at line 209.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/confirmation_service.py:98 — `    equipment.actual_data_status = ActualDataStatus.CONFIRMED.value` is the first statement of `pass_check`; the function body between its `def` (line 86) and this line contains no `if` on `actual_data_status`.

Executed against the real service with a stub session and an equipment row in `NOT_ENTERED`: `pass_check` returned with `status after pass_check on NOT_ENTERED: CONFIRMED committed: True`. The transition is reachable in isolation, with no designer step anywhere in the trace.
Executed `reject_check` against an equipment row in `CONFIRMED`: `CONFIRMED -> after reject: PENDING_CONFIRM`, i.e. a REVIEWER-only call re-opens the write channel on a locked record.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/confirmation_service.py:65-70 — the deviation gate `build_report` / `can_confirm` is called only inside `confirm_actual_data`; grepping the module for `PENDING_CONFIRM` returns only docstrings (lines 55, 56, 123, 124) and the two unconditional assignments, confirming no precondition exists on the check path.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add the state precondition inside the two service functions so it cannot be bypassed by any future caller, mirroring the existing `record_actual_data` pattern at `actual_data_service.py:92`:

```python
async def pass_check(session, equipment, actor, *, reason=""):
    if equipment.actual_data_status != ActualDataStatus.PENDING_CONFIRM.value:
        raise _error(
            "ACTUAL_DATA_NOT_SUBMITTED",
            f"实际数据未提交校核（当前状态 {equipment.actual_data_status}）—— "
            "须先由设计人录入并确认",
            status=409,
        )
    ...
```

Apply the same guard to `reject_check`. Note `confirm_actual_data` deliberately leaves the status at `PENDING_CONFIRM` (see its docstring at lines 55-57), so `PENDING_CONFIRM` is the correct and only legal precondition for both — a reviewer can accept or reject exactly the set of records a designer submitted, and nothing else. Assumption: the reviewer should not be able to act on a record whose designer-submission step was skipped; if the product intends otherwise, that intent needs to be written into SPEC §3.2.4(4) rather than left implicit.
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/supplier.py:210-212 — `    record = await _load_equipment(db, equipment_id, actor)` / `    if body.decision == "pass":` / `        await pass_check_svc(db, record, actor, reason=body.reason)`

findings.title: [A03/CWE-1236] Excel export writes the designer-controlled parameter name into a live formula cell — verified data_type 'f'
findings.why_it_matters: `ActualDataEntry.name` is an arbitrary string from the designer's PUT body (`Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)`, no character restriction). `build_report` iterates `for name in actual:` and every row's `parameter` field carries that string verbatim into the workbook. openpyxl does not escape a leading `=`, so the cell is persisted as a live formula. I confirmed this end to end: with `name = "=cmd|'/c calc'!A0"` the exported workbook round-trips as `B2 "=cmd|'/c calc'!A0" f` — `f` is openpyxl's formula data type. The attacker is any DESIGNER or PROCESS_CONTROLLER on the project (the export is VIEWER-gated, so the file reaches every viewer and any downstream recipient of the export); the victim is whoever opens the file in Excel, where the formula evaluates. On older Excel that is DDE / command execution; on current Excel the reliable payload is `=HYPERLINK(...)` or an external-cell-reference exfiltration of the workbook's own contents. Because the write role and the read role are different people here, this is a stored, cross-role delivery mechanism: a designer plants it, a viewer or process engineer trips it. The same unescaped value also reaches `unit` (column E) and, via `tag_number`, column A.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:206-219 — `wb.append([report.tag_number, row.parameter, row.design_value, row.actual_value, row.unit, ...])`; `row.parameter` is passed to openpyxl with no escaping or prefix.
pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:22 — `    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100, description="参数名")` — no pattern, no character class; `=` is accepted.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:84 — `for name in actual:` — the loop is over the JSONB keys, which are exactly the attacker-supplied `name` values after `normalize_entries` (`actual_data_service.py:71`, `out[name] = {...}`).

Executed export with `actual_data_json = {"=cmd|'/c calc'!A0": {"value": 1.0, "unit": ""}, ...}`; reloading the produced workbook with openpyxl printed `B2 "=cmd|'/c calc'!A0" f`. The `f` data type is openpyxl's marker for a formula cell — the payload is stored as executable formula, not as text.
findings.suggested_fix:
Neutralize formula-injection on every string cell before it reaches openpyxl. The standard OWASP mitigation is a leading-apostrophe prefix, which Excel renders as text and which round-trips safely:

```python
def _safe_cell(value):
    """防 CSV/Excel 公式注入 (CWE-1236): 前导 = + - @ 会被 Excel 当公式执行."""
    if isinstance(value, str) and value[:1] in ("=", "+", "-", "@", "\t", "\r"):
        return "'" + value
    return value
```

Apply `_safe_cell(...)` to `report.tag_number`, `row.parameter`, and `row.unit` in the `wb.append([...])` list at line 207. Prefixing is preferable to rejecting, because legitimate parameter names are Chinese engineering terms and the current `ActualDataEntry` validation deliberately does not constrain characters — validation would silently break existing callers for no security gain once the cell is inert. Assumption: the export is the sole sink for this value today; if a future consumer re-parses the xlsx, prefix-stripping will be needed there.
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:208 — `                row.parameter,` (inside the `wb.append([` list at line 207, written with no escaping)

findings.title: [A03/CWE-918] PDF export interpolates the designer-controlled parameter name into a reportlab Paragraph, which parses inline markup — local file open confirmed
findings.why_it_matters: `export_pdf` wraps every cell value in `reportlab.platypus.Paragraph`, whose default parser interprets a mini-HTML markup: ``, ``, ``, and notably ``, whose `src` is resolved by `reportlab.lib.utils.ImageReader`. Both `report.tag_number` (line 274) and `row.parameter` (line 277) come from designer-supplied strings. I confirmed the file-open primitive: exporting a report whose parameter name is `` produced `PDF ERR: UnidentifiedImageError ... fileName='/etc/hostname' identity=[ImageReader@0x7acf639ad` — the export path genuinely opened an attacker-named path on the server's filesystem. That is a local-file-read primitive (CWE-73) escalating to disclosure: any readable file that happens to parse as an image is embedded into the returned PDF and handed to the caller. `ImageReader` also accepts `http://` and `https://` URLs, which makes the same primitive an SSRF against internal-network services reachable from the backend. The realistic ceiling is bounded — the file must be a parseable image or the request 500s — but a request-issuing SSRF that 500s differently on reachable vs unreachable hosts is still an internal-network probe, and image-format assets on a file server are a normal thing to have. `row.note`, `row.spec_ref`, and `report.blocking_reason` reach `Paragraph` on the same terms, though those are currently engine-authored rather than user-authored.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:274-285 — `data.append([Paragraph(report.tag_number, cell_style), Paragraph(row.parameter, cell_style), Paragraph(str(row.design_value), cell_style), ...])` — raw `Paragraph(...)` with no escaping; reportlab's default paraparser handles inline markup in the argument.
pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:276 — `                Paragraph(row.parameter, cell_style),` is the sink, fed by the same attacker-controlled `name` identified in SEC-2.

Executed `export_pdf` with `actual_data_json = {"": {"value": 1.0, "unit": ""}}`; output was `PDF ERR: UnidentifiedImageError ... caused exception fileName='/etc/hostname' identity=[ImageReader@0x7acf639ad`. The `ImageReader@` identity confirms the path was opened by the export code, not merely echoed into an error string.

Confidence is 75 rather than 100 because I confirmed the local-file open but did not stand up an HTTP listener to confirm the `http://` SSRF variant; `reportlab.lib.utils.ImageReader` handles URLs through the same `open_for_read` path, but that specific leg rests on reportlab's documented behaviour rather than on an execution I ran.
findings.suggested_fix:
Escape the text before it becomes a `Paragraph`, so markup is rendered literally rather than interpreted. `reportlab.platypus.Paragraph` accepts an XML-escaped string, and `xml.sax.saxutils.escape` is already a stdlib dependency of reportlab:

```python
from xml.sax.saxutils import escape

data.append([
    Paragraph(escape(str(report.tag_number)), cell_style),
    Paragraph(escape(str(row.parameter)), cell_style),
    ...
])
```

Apply `escape()` to every `Paragraph(...)` argument in `export_pdf` — the tag number, parameter, design value, actual value, unit, deviation, label, colour, and note cells at lines 274-284, plus the `blocking_reason` at line 269 — not just the user-controlled ones, since the same helper is the right default for any cell that will ever carry free text. Assumption: no caller depends on markup being live in these cells; the header row at line 271 is static SPEC column names and can stay unescaped, though escaping it too is harmless.

findings.title: [A03/CWE-20] The strict-float contract on `ActualDataEntry.value` is enforced only by Pydantic's lax coercion, so the service's own string/bool rejection is unreachable dead code on the API path
findings.why_it_matters: Both the schema docstring ("value 严格数值 —— 字符串数字在 UI 上是录入错误, 不是可容忍的输入") and `actual_data_service._coerce_value` (docstring: "不接受 '100' 这类字符串数字", with an explicit `isinstance(raw, bool)` rejection) state that string numerics and booleans must be refused. Neither guard actually fires on the router path, because Pydantic v2 runs first in lax mode and hands the service an already-coerced `float`. Verified against the real schema: `'100' -> 100.0`, `True -> 1.0`, `'NaN' -> nan`, `'Infinity' -> inf`. So the service's boolean branch is unreachable from `PUT /actual-data` and the string-digit rule is not enforced at all. The security-relevant edge is that non-finite floats survive validation: `float('nan')` reaches `deviation_service.evaluate`, where every comparison against NaN is false, so the `ASYMMETRIC_BAND` rule falls through to `return Evaluation(QUALIFIED, deviation)` — I verified `can_confirm` returns `True` for a pump whose entire actual-data set is `{"扬程": {"value": NaN}}`, i.e. a value that was never measured would clear the SPEC §3.2.4(4) confirmation gate. That specific bypass does not reach production today: PostgreSQL 18.6 rejects `NaN` as a JSONB literal (`InvalidTextRepresentationError` on `select 'NaN'::jsonb`), so the write fails with a 500 rather than persisting — the practical impact today is an unhandled 500 on a request a client can trigger, not a confirmed forged value. I file it at P2 and 75 for that reason: the validation contract the code documents is not the contract the code enforces, and the moment a non-finite value becomes storable — or a numeric-typed column replaces the JSONB — the NaN-to-QUALIFIED path becomes live.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:23 — `    value: float = Field(description="实测值 (可为负, 如冬季设计温度)")` — a bare `float` with no `Field(strict=True)` and no `allow_inf_nan=False`.

Executed against the real `ActualDataEntry` model: `'100' -> 100.0`, `True -> 1.0`, `'NaN' -> nan`, `'Infinity' -> inf`, `None REJECT ValidationError`. Pydantic lax mode coerces the exact inputs that `actual_data_service.py:33-39` `_coerce_value` exists to reject.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/actual_data_service.py:35 — `    if isinstance(raw, bool) or not isinstance(raw, (int, float)):` — unreachable from the router, because `model_dump()` at `supplier.py:121` yields `value` as an already-coerced `float`.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:249 — `        return Evaluation(QUALIFIED, deviation)` is the fall-through of `ASYMMETRIC_BAND`; with `deviation = nan` both guards at lines 245 and 247 compare false, so execution lands here. Executed: `扬程 QUALIFIED nan` and `can_confirm = True` for `actual_data_json={'扬程':{'value':float('nan'),...}}` against a design value of 2100.0.

The persistence leg was checked against the live database and does not hold: `PostgreSQL 18.6`, `jsonb NaN ERR: asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidTextRepresentationError`. This is why severity is P2 rather than P0 — the gate bypass is demonstrable in-process but not yet reachable through stored data.
findings.suggested_fix:
Make the schema enforce the contract it documents, so the service-level checks become defence in depth rather than the only (unreachable) defence:

```python
value: float = Field(
    description="实测值 (可为负, 如冬季设计温度)",
    strict=True,
    allow_inf_nan=False,
)
```

`strict=True` rejects `'100'` and `True` at the boundary, matching both docstrings; `allow_inf_nan=False` closes the NaN/Infinity path into `evaluate` regardless of storage format. This is a breaking change for any client currently sending string numerics, which is precisely the behaviour the two docstrings say should not be tolerated — worth confirming against the frontend types (`pcs-frontend/src/types/api.d.ts` is in this diff) before applying. Assumption: no legitimate caller depends on lax numeric coercion; if one does, the fix is to fix that caller, not to widen the field.
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:23 — `    value: float = Field(description="实测值 (可为负, 如冬季设计温度)")`

residual_risks: `EventIdempotency.before_json` (pcs-backend/app/models/system.py:290) holds `design_parameters_json` snapshots with no `project_id` column, and `emit_event` writes it via a raw table-level select/insert (app/services/events.py:132-180) that bypasses the ORM relationship layer entirely. No read path for that table exists in this diff, so there is no exposure today — but if P8's reverse-recovery lands a query that selects `before_json` filtered on something other than the originating equipment, the table's lack of project scoping becomes a cross-project read. Worth a `project_id` column or an explicit note in the P8 plan.

The SYSTEM_ADMIN bypass in `check_project_access_or_404` (app/api/v1/_guard.py:39-40) is deliberate and pre-existing, documented at lines 33-36. I did not re-flag it. It does mean a SYSTEM_ADMIN can both `PUT /actual-data` and `POST /check` on the same record (SYSTEM_ADMIN appears in both `_WRITE_ROLES`/`_CONFIRM_ROLES` and `_CHECK_ROLES` at supplier.py:60-61, 175-176), collapsing four-eyes for that role — consistent with the existing bypass convention, so I left it alone, but it should be a conscious decision rather than a side effect of reusing the role tuples.

Role separation itself is correctly implemented: `_CHECK_ROLES = ("REVIEWER", "APPROVER", "SYSTEM_ADMIN")` contains no DESIGNER or PROCESS_CONTROLLER, so `/check` is unreachable by a submitter as the intent claims. Verified by reading supplier.py:175-176. The state-precondition gap in SEC-1 is the part that fails, not the role split.

`_load_equipment` (supplier.py:64-82) loads by `equipment_id` alone and then runs `check_project_access_or_404` before returning — I checked all six call sites (lines 102, 119, 157, 191, 210, 231) and every one reaches the guard before the record is touched. No path returns the row early. The 404-for-unauthorized semantics are correct and do not leak existence.

The `Content-Disposition` filename (supplier.py:241-251) is not injectable: `quote(record.tag_number, safe="")` percent-encodes CR, LF, and every other reserved character, and the ASCII fallback filename is the static `deviation-report.{ext}` rather than the tag. Header injection and path traversal via `tag_number` are both closed here.

`apply_design_parameters` (app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py:124-131) filters on both `EquipmentList.project_id == project_id` and `tag_number.in_(list(PUMP_DESIGN))`, so its writes are correctly project-scoped. Its only caller is the CLI script `scripts/p7_s4_003_seed_pump_design.py`, which requires an explicit `--project-id` argument. No authz surface, no finding.

Not reached within budget: I did not review `pcs-frontend/` beyond noting that `src/types/api.d.ts` is in the diff, and did not audit the two Alembic migrations (`p7_s4_001`, `p7_s4_002`) beyond confirming `EventIdempotency` has no project scoping column. The `EventIdempotency` model also has no relationship to `Project` or `EquipmentList`, so ORM-level query helpers cannot scope it today.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that `POST /actual-data/check` is rejected when `actual_data_status` is `NOT_ENTERED` or `CONFIRMED`. `tests/api/v1/test_actual_data_confirmation_api.py` sets up its fixture at line 54 with `actual_data_status="PENDING_CONFIRM"` and every check-path assertion runs from that state, so SEC-1 is invisible to the suite. Add two cases: check-pass on a `NOT_ENTERED` record → 409, and check-reject on a `CONFIRMED` record → 409.

No test exercises a hostile `ActualDataEntry.name`. The supplier service tests use engineering parameter names (扬程, 效率) only, which is why neither the formula-injection nor the markup-injection path is caught. Add an export test asserting that a name of `=1+1` round-trips from the workbook as a text cell (data_type `s`, not `f`), and one asserting `export_pdf` succeeds for a name containing ``.

No test asserts that `ActualDataEntry` rejects `'100'`, `True`, or `'NaN'`. The string-digit and boolean rules are documented in two docstrings and implemented in `actual_data_service`, but nothing pins the schema behaviour, so a future refactor to plain `float` would not fail a test.
